column1: # GWG Processing Steps Test Suite v1.0 — the expected-results table.
# INTERNAL REGRESSION EVIDENCE ONLY. Passing the gate that reads this table is
# not a Ghent Workgroup certification, and it is not an ISO 19593-1
# conformance claim: that standard is not held in this repository at all (the
# gap is recorded in src/engine/processing_steps.py, which names it). Nothing
# derived from this file may be worded as certified or as conforming.
# table, that script and the manifest are what the repository carries. Every
# `verdict` cell is PARAPHRASED from the suite's own documentation — which
# states the rule plainly: a patch whose name ends `G` must be accepted, one
# ending `E` must be rejected, one ending `W` is compliant but carries a setup
# that may be undesirable. Nothing here is a reading of what this product
# The suite's verdict is a PREFLIGHT verdict about the whole specification. A
# large part of that specification is not decidable here: the rules about
# z-order, colorant reuse, transparency, knock-out, image objects and
# off-bleed geometry each need the standard's own criteria, and guessing them
# would fail conforming files. Those rows are `not_applicable`: excluded from
# the verdict-agreement tally, never silently green, each carrying the rule
# the suite tests there. Their `steps` and `ps_inks` expectations still gate —
# what a document DECLARES is decidable whatever the rule about it says.
# The suite's documentation states 39 patches; the archive holds 40. It also
# documents a patch PS-012-03E (a custom step with no second class name) that
# the archive does not contain, so there is no row for it. Both are recorded
# here rather than reconciled: a row for an absent file would make the corpus
# permanently incomplete, and a corpus file with no row is a failure by
#   id        the patch id; its last letter is the suite's verdict class
#   patch     the file name under Patches/
#   verdict   good | error | warning, per the rule above
#   steps     what list_layers must report, as `Group/Type` (or `Group` for a
#             group that declares no type), in /OCGs order, `;`-separated
#   preflight the status the `processing_steps` check must report under the
#   ps_inks   the spot colorants list_inks must exclude as painted ONLY by
#   notes     for a not_applicable row, the rule the suite tests there
